These deities are believed to have the power to grant liberation from the cycle of birth and death and bestow boons upon their devotees. historical_references.reference: Mukunda, also known as Vishnu Avatar Matsya, is one of the ten incarnations of Lord Vishnu. He is believed to have appeared during the Satya Yuga, the first of the four stages of human civilization, to save the Earth from being flooded. The story begins when the king Manu, the progenitor of mankind, performs a great yajna (rite) to save the Earth from being destroyed by the demon Hiraanyaksha. During this yajna, the god Vishnu in the form of Matsya, the fish, appears to Manu and promises to save the Earth.

Another significant reference to Mukunda is in the Bhagavad Gita, where Lord Krishna is addressed as ‘Mukunda’ by Arjuna. Arjuna, disciple of Lord Krishna, is filled with grief over the impending war and the loss of his kinsmen. Lord Krishna reassures Arjuna and explains that those who take refuge in Him, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, attain liberation and attain the ultimate goal of life. Arjuna, consoled by Krishna’s words, addresses Him as Mukunda, meaning ‘the giver of salvation or liberation.’
